counting_rule: one candidate = one basic evaluate_elevation call, rejections included; a candidate may hold several rejection reasons, so reason occurrences and candidates-with-reason are reported separately and never summed into a candidate count
target_outcome_columns_note: old_D/new_D/old_E/new_E give the step status; the *_evaluations columns are after-minus-before for that target only (never the cumulative counter) and equal the number of candidate rows recorded for that target

unit_conversion_all.rule: start_shift_mm = start_shift_param x the primitive length; the parameter shift is bounded by 2*slack/length, so the millimetre shift is bounded by 2*slack

unit_conversion_relocation.rule: start_shift_mm = start_shift_param x the primitive length; the parameter shift is bounded by 2*slack/length, so the millimetre shift is bounded by 2*slack

match_uniqueness.note: a MATCHED row requires exactly one admissible candidate; several admissible candidates are recorded as AMBIGUOUS_MULTIPLE_MATCHES and are not forced into a match

accepted_edit_counts.note: passing acceptance is not execution: only the selected winner of a step is executed

executed edits are counted from the ledgers: D 8 and E 9, 17 in total. These are executed modifications, not the number of candidates that passed acceptance (143 matched rows passed the basic evaluation and 139 of those passed full acceptance).

benefit_decomposition.explanation: the route-34 relocation directly removes 26 pairs; the first elevations of routes 0, 1, 13 each create one fewer new pair (3 in total), which sums to the 29-pair difference

length_consistency.note: the single relocation step and the terminal D/E extra-length difference are the same quantity: only route 34 changes length in E relative to D
